children: TOKYO--Japan's consumer inflation picked up in September, backing the case for the central bank to raise interest rates again by the end of the year.

Consumer prices, excluding fresh food, climbed 2.1% in September from a year earlier, compared with August's 1.7% rise, government data showed Friday. That matched the forecast in a poll of economists by data provider Quick.
The results will likely reinforce market views that the Bank of Japan will tighten policy settings in December, bringing the benchmark rate up by another 25 basis points to 1.5%.
The bank's policy board is widely expected to stand pat when it gathers next week as it examines the effects of previous hikes, including in September.
A persistently weak yen and higher global oil prices are raising the cost of imported raw materials, keeping steady upward pressure on consumer prices in Japan.
Now that underlying inflation is very close to the bank's 2% target, BOJ Gov. Kazuo Ueda has said the central bank has to pay extra attention to upside risks to price growth.
